name: Poison Exon Blocking (Targeted Augmentation of Nuclear Gene Output; TANGO)
therapeuticGoalDescription: Increase endogenous protein expression by preventing inclusion of poison (non-productive) exons that trigger nonsense-mediated decay (NMD).
molecularDefect: Haploinsufficiency caused by excessive inclusion of poison exons or other non-productive splicing events that reduce productive mRNA.
diseaseMechanism: Inclusion of a poison exon introduces a premature termination codon, leading to nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and reduced protein production. Blocking poison exon inclusion restores productive mRNA and increases protein expression.
suitableVariantTypes: Haploinsufficiency; pathogenic deep intronic variants promoting poison exon inclusion; splice-regulatory variants affecting poison exon usage.
typicalDiseases: Dravet syndrome (SCN1A); Autosomal dominant optic atrophy (OPA1, investigational); SYNGAP1-related disorders (preclinical).
rnaTargetRegion: Poison exon sequence; flanking splice donor/acceptor sites; intronic splicing regulatory elements within pre-mRNA.
transcriptRequirement: Presence of a characterized poison exon or non-productive alternative splicing event in the target gene.
asoChemistry: RNase H-inactive steric-blocking ASOs; published studies commonly use fully modified 2′-MOE phosphorothioate oligonucleotides.
typicalLength: Approximately 18–20 nucleotides in published TANGO studies; no universal length has been established.
designRules: Literature synthesis: target splice-regulatory elements controlling poison exon inclusion; use steric-blocking chemistry; avoid RNase H activation; experimentally validate splice correction.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Target accessible splice-regulatory regions within pre-mRNA to maximize ASO binding and splice modulation.
offTargetConsiderations: Unintended modulation of alternative splicing in non-target transcripts; evaluate transcriptome-wide splice effects and sequence specificity.
advantages: Increases expression from the endogenous healthy allele; preserves physiological gene regulation; directly addresses haploinsufficiency.
limitations: Applicable only when a therapeutically targetable poison exon or non-productive splicing event exists; requires detailed transcript annotation and splice biology.
clinicalTrialExamples: STK-001 (zorevunersen) for Dravet syndrome; STK-002 for autosomal dominant optic atrophy (investigational). (stoketherapeutics.com)

evidenceLevel.note: Strong mechanistic evidence; clinical development ongoing but no FDA approval yet.
